html:
The Severians were an early East Slavic tribe living east of the middle Dnieper, along the Desna, Seym and Sula rivers, in what is now northeast Ukraine. They are on the map for 700.

They are named by the Bavarian Geographer in the 800s, by Emperor Constantine VII and in the Primary Chronicle. Their towns included Chernihiv and Novhorod-Siverskyi, and the region is still called Siveria. For a time they paid tribute to the Khazars. In the 880s Oleg made them pay tribute to Kyiv instead, and they became part of Kievan Rus'. Their neighbours to the west were the Polans of Kyiv.
